$comment: Every source SeniorSec reads. tier: foundation = shapes the rules; primary = authoritative facts that can confirm a finding or trigger a plan; news = leads only, must be confirmed against a primary source before anything changes. See sources/README.md for how they are combined.

sources.name: Clouds Against Humanity wiki
sources.notes: About 180 long pages. Do not read whole. Use sources/wiki-index.md to find the page for a topic.

sources.name: MITRE ATLAS
sources.notes: Technique IDs (AML.Txxxx) used in guide/ai-agents.md. Re-check IDs on each ATLAS release.

sources.name: OWASP Top 10:2025 (web applications)
sources.use: Category names behind the web-app pack.

sources.name: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard
sources.use: Testable requirements; use to make a rule's Check more precise.

sources.name: NIST SP 800-218 Secure Software Development Framework
sources.use: Practice IDs for the core pack. Version 1.1 is final; a 1.2 draft exists.

sources.name: NIST SP 800-218A SSDF profile for generative AI
sources.use: Second reference for the ai-agents pack alongside OWASP and ATLAS.

sources.name: CWE Top 25 Most Dangerous Software Weaknesses
sources.use: Weakness IDs for cross-referencing rules and advisories.

sources.name: OpenSSF Scorecard
sources.use: Repository hygiene checks that back CORE-06 and AI-05.

sources.name: OSV.dev
sources.notes: Aggregates GitHub Security Advisories, PyPA, RustSec and others. Query by package and version.

sources.name: GitHub Advisory Database
sources.notes: Reviewed advisories only. Already included in OSV results; use directly for detail pages.

sources.name: NIST National Vulnerability Database
sources.use: CVE record, CVSS vector and affected configurations. Second opinion on severity.

sources.name: FIRST Exploit Prediction Scoring System
sources.use: Probability a CVE is exploited in the next 30 days. Orders the queue after KEV. Query with ?cve=CVE-...,CVE-...

sources.name: CISA cybersecurity advisories
sources.use: Government confirmation and mitigations for active campaigns.

sources.name: Wordfence Intelligence vulnerability feed
sources.use: WordPress core, plugin and theme vulnerabilities. Free, but version 3 of the feed needs a free API key.

sources.name: AI Incident Database
sources.use: Real-world AI failures and abuse; leads for the ai-agents pack.
